transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-23
Start: 09:30 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood CSM); Carlos Rivera (BBH), Priya Sharma (BBH), Elena Rossi (BBH Sec PM), Michael O'Neal (BBH SRE)

Summary: Quick weekly POC check-in focusing on staging access readiness, initial benchmark results, quantization profile tradeoffs, and outstanding security items. Agreed next steps include raw benchmark upload, SOC2 docs share, firewall IP confirmation, and a deeper latency triage session.

Topics: onboarding progress, credentials & gateway readiness, staging performance numbers, quantization profile 'q4_eco' vs 'int8_perf', KV/prefix cache behavior, routing/fallback policies, SOC2/KMS questions.

Action items (short): see metadata action_items.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll keep this tight, 45-ish mins. Quick roll call?
[00:03] Carlos: Yeah Carlos here, ML lead, good morning.
[00:05] Priya: Priya, platform. We just landed the initial VPC peering yesterday.
[00:07] Elena: Elena, security PM.
[00:08] Michael: Michael, SRE, hello.
[00:10] Maya: Great. Ethan from our infra team is with me—Ethan, you want to call out the agenda?
[00:13] Ethan: Sure, real quick. We'll run through the bootstrapped benchmarks you sent, talk about the q4_eco quant profile results, check creds/gateway status, and then triage a p95 latency spike you flagged on Tuesday.
[00:22] Carlos: Cool. We pushed a small set of synthetic prompts and some real user prompts — uploaded to the shared drive. There were some odd p95s around 1.8 to 2.4 seconds which is higher than expected for 1k tokens.
[00:30] Ethan: Yeah I saw that — quick note, our staging was running the q4_eco profile which is 4-bit asymmetric quant, aimed at cost savings, so there's some variance. Can I ask what model variant you were calling?
[00:38] Carlos: We were on rwd-ggml-2.7b v3 (the one you recommended).
[00:42] Ethan: Okay that tracks. q4_eco helps on throughput but p95 can jump if batching/kv cache misses happen. I suspect a KV—people write it as K-V cash—cache warmup issue.
[00:50] Priya: On creds — staging API creds were created and shared with Redwood's gateway IP, but we still need the static egress IPs nailed down for our firewall. Also NAT is behind a managed gateway so IPs change after redeployments unless pinned.
[01:02] Maya: Understood — we'll give you the list of staging egress IPs for the gateway. I'll include a note about our fallback routing: if Dedicated pool saturated, requests route to lowest-cost compatible variant in the same region unless you pin.
[01:15] Elena: Quick security question — KMS integration: are keys stored in our keyring or Redwood-managed KMS? We need clarity for compliance audit.
[01:22] Ethan: You can do either. For Private deployments we'd use your KMS; for Hosted we offer customer-managed keys via KMS integration or HSM on enterprise tier. I'll send the KMS integration doc.
[01:31] Michael: For the staging bench, can you confirm what network egress bandwidth you observed? We saw some TCP retries during the p95 spike.
[01:38] Ethan: We logged small retransmits — looks like a short-lived spike around 09:15 PT when a background batch job kicked off. That caused a queueing delay in the nginx front proxy; we're looking at smoothing policies. Not a model execution issue per se.
[01:48] Carlos: That matches our logs. The spike aligns w/ our nightly ETL. Maybe we need a maintenance window or rate-limits during the bench.
[01:56] Maya: For bench validity, two notes: 1) run tests isolated from heavy ETL or use dedicated reserved pool; 2) ensure KV/prefix cache is warmed — run a quick prefix set of calls to populate cache.
[02:08] Priya: How do we warm the prefix cache? Is there a script?
[02:11] Ethan: We have a script in the repo (redwood/bench/warm_cache.sh) — I'll attach it. Essentially replay a representative prompt set at low concurrency before the main run.
[02:19] Carlos: Okay we'll do that. About quant profiles — we tried q4_eco and int8_perf. q4 was cheaper but quality seemed slightly off on some hallucination-sensitive prompts. Any guidance?
[02:31] Ethan: Yep, tradeoff. q4_eco reduces memory and cost but can alter numeric stability and subtle token distributions — for sensitive outputs recommend int8_perf or the new q3h_safe when latency SLOs are tight. We should run side-by-side quality evals (20-30 gold prompts).
[02:43] Elena: Is q3h_safe still experimental? We can't ship regressions for clinical-ish replies.
[02:47] Ethan: It's been vetted but flagged as "experimental" in the docs — we'll mark it as dogfood only. For compliance, use int8_perf for POC until you're comfortable.
[02:56] Maya: Also want to flag routing/fallback — you can pin model versions for canary rollouts. If a model variant fails we'll fall back to a pinned compatible variant, not to a public one. That's in the rollout policy.
[03:07] Carlos: Good. On the p95 numbers — our target is p50 < 500ms and p95 < 1.2s for 1k tokens. Right now p50 is 320ms, p95 1.9s on staging.
[03:18] Ethan: Two immediate levers: batch sizing and prefix cache. Increasing batch size reduces per-token cost but can raise tail latencies if concurrency is uneven. Another is to enable low-latency short-path for high-priority tokens (we can prioritize your signed token set).
[03:33] Priya: Can we turn on a short-path for a specific route only? We want dev to use normal settings, prod to have low-latency.
[03:38] Maya: Yes, per-route SLOs and overrides are supported. We can give staging different policy bindings so your prod route can pin to Dedicated pool with strict latency SLOs.
[03:47] Michael: Any recommendations on autoscale policy for Dedicated? We saw some cold starts that look like model load time.
[03:52] Ethan: We recommend keeping at least 1 warm replica per model for predictable SLOs or use image pre-warm hooks. Also set burst capacity to handle sudden 2-5x spikes. The load time you saw matches the model load times for 2.7b under cold start — ~700ms to 1s.
[04:06] Carlos: That would eat our budget if we keep warm replicas. Can we do a hybrid approach? Warm for high-priority routes only.
[04:10] Maya: Absolutely — that's the typical pattern. Warm the prod route, keep dev/staging on demand.
[04:14] Jordan: Quick note — I'll open a support ticket for the p95 trace and cc the group so we can attach the raw span logs.
[04:19] Carlos: Thanks. About credentials — we tried rotating API keys and saw a denied call during rotation window. Is there a recommended rotation flow?
[04:26] Ethan: Use dual-key rollout: create new key, update apps to start using new key, then revoke old key; Redwood supports key status with a 30s grace period for in-flight calls. Also you can use short-lived tokens via our token service for better rotation.
[04:38] Priya: We'll aim to switch to short-lived tokens for staging next week.
[04:41] Maya: Okay, next steps recap — I'll share SOC2 + KMS + RBAC summary and the warm_cache script; Ethan will run and upload the 1k/4k token bench; Priya will confirm firewall egress IPs. We also want the canonical prompt set from Carlos so we can run quality evals across q4_eco/int8_perf.
[04:58] Carlos: I'll push the prompt set and a little readme to the shared drive after this call.
[05:03] Elena: One more compliance question — audit logs: do you provide per-request redaction or token-level redaction controls for PII?
[05:10] Ethan: We support configurable redaction in the pipeline and can store audit logs in your account for the Private deployment. For Hosted, we provide redaction hooks and encrypted logs; we'll send the audit-log spec.
[05:19] Maya: Anything else?
[05:21] Michael: Not from SRE. We'll coordinate the ETL maintenance window for the next bench.
[05:25] Priya: We'll update firewall rules and share terraform snippet.
[05:28] Maya: Great. Thanks everyone — I'll send notes and links within 24 hours and sync the deep-dive for next week.
[05:34] Carlos: Thanks all.
[05:36] (meeting ends)
